private_source.inspection: Scoped manual reading of Tables 1-2, Sections 2.3-2.4, 3.1-3.2 and 4, Figure 4, and the supporting-information notice. Equations, figure labels and table units were also checked on rendered pages. Supplementary data and Shelby (1994) were not supplied or inspected. Replaying this review does not repeat source inspection.

evidence.summary: The basalt regression printed in Hirschmann (2012), Figure 4, is ln K = -11.403 - 0.76 P(GPa), with K = X_H2/f_H2 and f_H2 in bar.
evidence.scope: Published regression, concentration convention and reference conditions only. This is not an independent reconstruction of the fit or validation of its inherited calibration, fugacity model or application to another melt.

provenance.location: Printed p. 40, Table 2 heading and footnote c; p. 42, Section 4, Eq. 6; p. 43, Figure 4 label and caption (PDF pages 3, 5, 6).
provenance.note: Read on 2026-10-19. X_H2 uses an oxide-component mole basis including H2O. Exponentiating the printed basalt regression gives X_H2 = f_H2_bar * exp(-11.403 - 0.76 * P_GPa); no additional pressure-reference shift is applied to this empirical line. The general thermodynamic Eq. 6 uses T0 = 1400 degC (1673.15 K), P0 = 100 kPa, and enthalpy and volume terms. The authors could not calibrate the enthalpy term from their temperature spread; absence of temperature in the adopted regression does not establish temperature independence. Figure 4 attributes calculated fugacities to Zhang and Duan (2009) and compositions to supplementary data, neither reconstructed here.

evidence.summary: Table 1 separates basalt + COH runs at 1400-1450 degC and 0.7-3 GPa from andesite + OH runs at 1400-1500 degC and 1-3 GPa.
evidence.scope: Marginal envelopes of the two Table 1 series, plus explicitly identified exclusions; not a continuous joint calibration domain or a complete machine-readable run inventory.

provenance.location: Printed p. 39, Table 1; p. 40, Table 2; p. 42, Section 3.1 continuation (PDF pages 2, 3, 5).
provenance.note: Read on 2026-10-19. Adding 273.15 gives basalt 1673.15-1723.15 K and andesite 1673.15-1773.15 K. Basalt A697/A711 are the 1450 degC runs, both at 1.5 GPa. Andesite A950/A949 are at 1500 degC, at 2/2.5 GPa. Section 3.1 excludes black andesite glasses A882/A950 from thermodynamic calibration; retained A949 still reaches 1500 degC. Table 2 marks basalt B340 H2 as n.d.; no numeric concentration is inferred. Total melt pressure is distinct from the calculated H2 fugacity. Buffers and material labels were read, but detailed compositions require the missing supplementary data.

evidence.summary: Hirschmann (2012) explicitly adopts a SiO2-glass infrared calibration from Shelby (1994) because an aluminosilicate calibration was unavailable.
evidence.scope: Directly inspected adoption and the authors' uncertainty discussion. The earlier calibration's numeric value, definition, original determination and transferability remain unaudited.

provenance.location: Printed p. 40, Section 2.4; p. 42, Section 3.2 and Figure 3; p. 47, Shelby reference (PDF pages 3, 5, 10).
provenance.note: Read on 2026-10-19. Section 2.4 attributes the adopted integrated absorption coefficient to Shelby; it does not print the 0.26 value reported by the later paper. Section 3.2 warns of potentially greater than 100% uncertainty from silica-to-mafic transfer, then suggests perhaps +/-50% from the SIMS/FTIR comparison. These are the authors' estimates, not an uncertainty model for the implemented function. No universal correction using the 2025 coefficient is established.

derived_from.note: The adoption in 2012 is now directly inspected. Shelby (1994) itself remains uninspected, including coefficient convention and calibration transfer.

evidence.summary: Seo (2024), Eq. 6 reproduces the published basalt regression; the preceding temperature interval agrees with basalt Table 1 values at whole-kelvin precision.
evidence.scope: Expression, bar/GPa units, reported mole-fraction output, and basalt temperature envelope only. No downstream melt-composition or concentration-conversion audit.

provenance.location: arXiv:2408.17056v1, Section II.3, Eq. 6, variable definitions and preceding paragraph.
provenance.note: Re-read on 2026-10-19 and compared with the supplied 2012 full text. The original explicitly defines the oxide-component basis; Seo calls the result a mole fraction. Equating atmospheric pressure with actual melt pressure remains a boundary-model assumption.

derived_from.note: Exponentiation of the printed Figure 4 basalt line gives Seo Eq. 6 with the same numeric coefficients and bar/GPa conventions. This closes formula transcription only, not independent regression or physical validation.

Seo's 1673-1723 K matches the basalt envelope when converted temperatures are rounded to integer kelvin. The 0.15 K difference is retained in separate Conditions and is not evidence of experimental temperature precision.

conditions.scope: Table 1 basalt + COH temperature envelope, converted from degC. No interpolation, material matching or uncertainty tolerance is inferred.
Table 1 andesite + OH temperature envelope; A949 retains the upper bound after A950 is excluded. This does not extend the basalt law.
Table 1 basalt + COH total-pressure envelope only, not hydrogen fugacity or a joint T/P domain.
Table 1 andesite + OH total-pressure envelope only; the study-wide 0.7 GPa minimum belongs to basalt.

physical_assessment_reasons: The published coefficient ancestry is now inspected; the retained physical_accuracy proposition still lacks a specified observable and tolerance.

The requested 1750 K is above the basalt Table 1 envelope. The andesite temperature envelope includes it, but 7500 bar is below the andesite pressure envelope; the two materials cannot be combined into one applicability rectangle.
Melt composition and hydrogen fugacity are unspecified. Published f_H2 values are model-derived; supplementary compositions and the underlying fugacity calculation have not been reconstructed.

The adopted Shelby calibration and its transfer remain unresolved. Published calibration data and a consistent formula transcription do not independently validate this calculation; no new measurement comparison or correction was made.
